claim.pdf_says: READ statement, Format 2 (random): the INVALID KEY / NOT INVALID KEY group is printed as a tall BRACKET with a pair of vertical CHOICE-INDICATOR BARS just inside it, spanning both stacked alternatives:  [|  INVALID KEY imperative-statement-3  |]  /  [|  NOT INVALID KEY imperative-statement-4  |]
claim.markdown_says:
[ [ INVALID KEY imperative-statement-3     ] ]
  [ [ NOT INVALID KEY imperative-statement-4 ] ]
[ END-READ ]
claim.why_it_matters: Same defect class as the Format 1 AT END group: the 5.2.6.4 choice indicators were replaced by a nested bracket, which reads as 'at most one of INVALID KEY / NOT INVALID KEY'. The standard permits BOTH on one READ, and GR 13 c (page 726) relies on that. The transcription renders this identical construct correctly for DELETE (specs/ISO_COBOL.md:26323-26324) and for the START/REWRITE/WRITE family (:30094, :31754, :32999).

verdict.reasoning:
Independently confirmed by rendering page 722 at 300 dpi (E:/Temp/specrecon/v722/spec_p722.png) and inspecting the INVALID KEY group glyph-by-glyph at 8x magnification (crops z_left.png / z_right.png).

WHAT THE PRINTED GLYPHS ACTUALLY ARE. At the left edge of the group there are TWO distinct vertical strokes. The outer one has a short horizontal arm at its top and another at its bottom, both pointing RIGHT (into the group) - that is a left square bracket. Immediately to its right is a second vertical stroke with NO horizontal arms at either end, and it is visibly TALLER than the bracket, overshooting it both above and below - that is a plain bar, i.e. a choice indicator. The right edge is the mirror image: first a plain armless vertical bar (again taller, overshooting the bracket), then a stroke with top and bottom arms pointing LEFT, i.e. a right square bracket. Both bars span the full two-line stack (INVALID KEY on line 1, NOT INVALID KEY on line 2). So the printed construct is unambiguously [ | ...stack... | ] - an outer bracket pair enclosing a choice-indicator pair. The claim's description of the PDF is exactly right. For calibration, the KEY IS group immediately above on the same page shows a bare bracket with no adjacent armless stroke, so the extra bars in the INVALID KEY group are not a rendering artifact of the bracket glyph.

WHAT THE MARKDOWN ACTUALLY SAYS. specs/ISO_COBOL.md:29483-29485 reads verbatim '  [ [ INVALID KEY imperative-statement-3     ] ]' / '  [ [ NOT INVALID KEY imperative-statement-4 ] ]' / '[ END-READ ]'. The claim quotes it exactly. The bars are gone; a second bracket pair stands in their place. There is no compensating figure note anywhere near the block - line 29486 closes the fence, 29488 is 'where retry-phrase is described in 14.7.9, RETRY phrase'. So nothing restores the lost semantics.

WHY THE SUBSTITUTION CHANGES MEANING (not mere formatting). 5.2.6.2 (specs/ISO_COBOL.md:2693): brackets indicate 'the syntax element contained within the brackets OR ONE OF THE ALTERNATIVES contained within the brackets may be explicitly specified' - i.e. at most one of a stack. 5.2.6.4 (:2703): 'Choice indicators are a pair of bars, |, that enclose a portion of a general format. ... When enclosed by brackets, ZERO OR MORE of the alternatives contained within the choice indicators shall be specified, but any single alternative may be specified only once. ... The alternatives may be specified in any order.' Bracket-over-a-stack and bars-over-a-stack are therefore normatively DIFFERENT quantifiers: at-most-one versus any-subset. The transcription's inner bracket is not a typographic variant of a bar, it states a strictly narrower syntax.

The ambiguity defence does not rescue it either. Within this very figure the transcription uses repeated per-line delimiters to denote ONE tall delimiter spanning a stack - '{ NEXT }' / '{ PREVIOUS }' at :29454-29455 and '{ data-name-1 }' / '{ record-key-name-1 }' at :29480-29481. Read under the transcription's own convention, '[ [ X ] ]' / '[ [ Y ] ]' is one tall outer bracket wrapping one tall inner bracket wrapping two stacked alternatives, which is precisely the at-most-one reading. A conforming READ carrying both INVALID KEY and NOT INVALID KEY would be rejected by an implementer working from the markdown.

THE CONSEQUENCE CITATION CHECKS OUT. READ GR 13 (found in the READ general rules following the formats) reads 'If neither an at end nor an invalid key condition occurs during the execution of a READ statement, the AT END phrase or the INVALID KEY phrase is ignored, if specified, and the following actions occur:' with 'c) ... Control is transferred to the end of the READ statement, or, if the NOT AT END phrase or NOT INVALID KEY phrase is specified, to imperative-statement-2.' That rule describes ignoring a specified INVALID KEY phrase while simultaneously branching to a specified NOT INVALID KEY imperative statement, which presupposes both phrases coexisting on one READ. The claim's 'GR 13 c ... relies on that' is accurate.

THE INTERNAL-INCONSISTENCY EVIDENCE CHECKS OUT. The identical construct is transcribed WITH its bars elsewhere in the same file: REWRITE at :30094 and START at :31754 and WRITE at :32999 all read '⎡ | INVALID KEY imperative-statement-1     | ⎤' / '⎣ | NOT INVALID KEY imperative-statement-2 | ⎦'. DELETE at :26323-26324 also retains bars, though in a cruder form ('⌐ INVALID KEY ... ¬' / '| NOT INVALID KEY ... |', where the corner glyphs stand in for the bracket arms) - so the cleanest exemplars are the REWRITE/START/WRITE trio rather than DELETE. Either way the claim's point stands: READ Format 2 is the outlier.

I attempted every refutation route and none held. The bars are not present-but-reflowed - they are absent from the block and from the whole page slice. The difference is not page-break furniture, wrapping, or hyphenation - it is a delimiter substitution inside a general format. Neither source is misquoted. And the difference does change meaning, by the spec's own 5.2.6.2-versus-5.2.6.4 definitions. The sibling AT END defect in Format 1 at :29464-29465 is present too and is real for the same reasons, consistent with the claim calling this the same defect class.
verdict.corrected_description: Confirmed as described; no correction to the substance. Two refinements for the ledger. (1) The lost markup is a single pair of choice-indicator bars spanning the whole two-alternative stack, sitting just inside one tall outer bracket pair - i.e. one bracket group plus one bar group, not a per-line delimiter on each row; the markdown's per-line '[ ... ]' repetition is its normal way of drawing one tall delimiter, which is why it reads as a nested bracket rather than as two independent options. (2) Among the cited correct exemplars, REWRITE (:30094), START (:31754) and WRITE (:32999) are the clean ones, using '⎡ | ... | ⎤ / ⎣ | ... | ⎦'; DELETE (:26323-26324) preserves the bars but draws the outer bracket with corner glyphs ('⌐ ... ¬'), so it is a weaker precedent. The fix for READ Format 2 is to restore the bars in the REWRITE/START/WRITE form, and the same fix applies to the AT END group of READ Format 1 at :29464-29465.
